notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 06/18/2026
Patient: Candice Kozey, 81-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 06/18/2026. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 30.9 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 12% of all events. The study showed a predominance of obstructive events contributing to the overall apnea-hypopnea index. Oxygen saturation levels demonstrated intermittent desaturations associated with respiratory events. Sleep architecture was preserved with normal distribution of REM and non-REM sleep stages. No significant cardiac arrhythmias or periodic limb movements were observed during the recording. These findings indicate moderate to severe sleep apnea requiring clinical correlation and consideration for appropriate management.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/18/2026
Patient: Candice Kozey, 81-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation of sleep disturbances and assessment for possible sleep apnea.

History:
Ms. Kozey reports frequent nighttime awakenings and non-restorative sleep. She denies excessive daytime sleepiness but notes occasional morning headaches. No history of restless legs or periodic limb movements.

Physical Examination:
Vital signs are stable. BMI 31.7 kg/m2. No craniofacial abnormalities noted. Oropharyngeal examination reveals mild tonsillar hypertrophy.

Assessment:
Obesity is a contributing factor to her sleep complaints. Further evaluation with polysomnography is recommended to assess for sleep-disordered breathing.

Plan:
Schedule overnight sleep study. Counsel on sleep hygiene and weight management strategies. Follow-up after diagnostic testing to discuss results and management options.

notes.author: Otolaryngologist
notes.text:
Otolaryngology Consultation Note
Date: 09/26/2026
Patient: Candice Kozey, 81-year-old female

This 81-year-old woman referred for hypoglossal nerve stimulation evaluation. Drug-induced sleep endoscopy 09/18/2026: anteroposterior collapse at the velum without complete concentric collapse. Oropharynx: tonsils size 1, no other anatomic obstruction. No neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal palsy, severe cardiopulmonary disease or planned MRI; able to operate the sleep remote.

Based on these findings, the patient appears to be an appropriate candidate for hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy. The plan is to proceed with further evaluation and preparation for implantation. The patient will be counseled on device use and follow-up arranged accordingly.
